nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman spectroscopy shows for NiFe LDH weak peaks at 461 cm⁻¹ (e_g bending) and 535 cm⁻¹ (A_{1g} stretching) of Ni(OH)₂; early α/γ transition to γ-NiFeOOH at 1.35 V in alkaline seawater vs 1.4 V in pure water.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For NiFe LDH measured in alkaline pure water, as the anodic potential rises to 1.4 V the new peaks at 477 cm⁻¹ and 556 cm⁻¹ replace the initial two peaks ... In comparison, an early appearance of α/γ transition was observed in alkaline seawater (e.g., 1.35 V, Figure 2b)

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ XAS shows Fe K-edge shift decreases to 0.45 eV and Ni K-edge reaches maximum in alkaline seawater at 1.6 V; clear Fe-Cl peak in FT-EXAFS after 1.45 V confirms Cl⁻ adsorption on Fe site.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In k³-weighted Fourier transformed extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra (Figure 3b), a clear Fe-Cl peak can be observed in alkaline seawater after the potential reaches 1.45 V, which indicates the adsorption of Cl⁻ species on the Fe site.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p shows Ni³⁺ peak at 857.6 eV (Ni 2p_{3/2}) constituting 28% after stability test in alkaline seawater.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the reduced leaching of Fe allowed a greater amount of Ni³⁺ (857.6 eV, Ni 2p_{3/2}) to retain after the test (constituting 28%)

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS shows dissolved Ni 140.3 ng mL⁻¹ and Fe 35.15 ng mL⁻¹ in alkaline seawater after stability test; Ni:Fe ratio remains similar unlike pure water.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the minimum amount of dissolved Ni (140.3 ng mL⁻¹) and Fe ions (35.15 ng mL⁻¹) are found in alkaline seawater
